sections.en: 1 On Apomasar (i.e. Abu-Ma'shar), an astrologer most famous in the age of the caliph Al-Mamun, who died in the year 885 A.D., cf. Usener, Ad historiam astronomiae symbola, 1876, p. 21; Steinschneider, Die hebräischen Uebersetzungen des Mittelalters, II, Berlin, 1893, p. 566 ss.; Krumbacher, Byz. Litg., ed. 2, p. 630.— In this astrological book, which we have inspected, the precepts of Apomasar have been mixed together by a certain compiler with doctrines sought from elsewhere.

summary.headline: Apomasar’s Astrological Chapters
summary.text: Chapter list from the astrological book of Apomasar, with folio references, covering cosmic outcomes, solar and lunar eclipses, the chronocrator, abundance and scarcity, heatwaves, Mercury’s affliction, the Harranian method and cosmic year, the rising of the Dog Star, rains, winds, and the constitution of the universe. The catalog notes that the Laurentian codex was copied from Angelicanus 29 and that Apomasar’s teachings were mixed with material from other sources.
